data.title: Fed's table is set for a rate hike, a first underÂ Warsh
data.description:
Sept 14 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh dislikes giving any guidance about the likely path of U.S. interest rates, but elevated inflation, $100-a-barrel oil, and his own emphasis on the need to deliver price stability and to pay attention to signals from financial market pricing appear to leave little doubt about what's next. 

The U.S. central bank will announce its policy decision at 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT) on Wednesday following the end of a two-day meeting. Financial markets are betting heavily that Fed policymakers will lift their benchmark rate a quarter of a percentage point, to a 3.75%-4.00% range, and signal further tightening ahead.  

Such a decision could land Warsh, who has run the Fed's rate-setting committee since starting the job in May, in a tight place. President Donald Trump picked Warsh with the explicit expectation that he would cut interest rates, but so far has not blamed him for failing to deliver, saying it is the fault of his "political" fellow central bankers. It's not clear how the president would react to a rate hike so soon before November elections in which Trump's Republican party is defending slim majorities in Congress.

A decision to raise rates, especially if accompanied by policymaker projections for another increase this year as some analysts now expect, could also force Warsh into delivering at least a bit of a steer on the rate path and his own expectations for the economy  -- unless he is comfortable with leaving the door wide open to further increases. 

"Warsh will also need to walk a fine line in his remarks if he still aims to provide no forward guidance," TD Securities economist Oscar Munoz wrote. "If the Fed decides to tighten policy, he will certainly be asked about future rate hikes. It is fairly clear to us that more tightening would be in the pipeline if the Fed goes the hiking route in September. It will be interesting to see how the chairman goes through that balancing act."

A week ago, there was far less certainty about this week's outcome.

"Give disinflation a chance," quipped Fed Governor Christopher Waller at a REUTERS NEXT event in early September, citing cooler inflation readings in June and July that appeared to carve a path toward the Fed's 2% goal within a reasonable time frame.  "I think that we have to wait and see," New York Fed President John Williams said earlier this month. 

But hotter-than-expected inflation readings last week may disappoint both Williams and Waller, and add to the dismay of the three regional Fed bank presidents -- Cleveland Fed's Beth Hammack, Dallas Fed's Lorie Logan, and Minneapolis Fed's Neel Kashkari -- who already in July felt the Fed ought to be raising rates and dissented on the decision to hold steady instead. Several other Fed policymakers have said they need to see disinflation "soon" or they too would support a rate hike.

U.S. consumer price inflation excluding energy and food, a key measure of underlying inflation, rose 0.3% last month from the previous month, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported, far more than is consistent with inflation at the Fed's 2% goal. Coupled with oil prices that have soared above $100 a barrel amid renewed hostilities in the Middle East, the latest data won't add to confidence that underlying inflation is moving toward 2% "clearly and at sufficient speed," as Warsh told global central bankers in Jackson Hole, Wyoming last month that he wanted to see.

"At the end of the day the chair's repeated stern warnings on inflation intolerance risk institutional credibility absent some action to back it up," said JPMorgan economist Michael Feroli, who projects the Fed will raise rates on Wednesday although he thinks it's a "closer call" than the 85% chance or so priced in by futures markets.

Scotiabank economist Derek Holt believes hiking rates now is the wrong move but thinks it will happen regardless, given what Warsh said. "Chair Warsh has probably boxed himself in with his high deference to markets," Holt said. "If you don't hike when it's priced, then when?"

Economists say that with most Fed policymakers likely to defer to the preferences of the still-new Fed chair, Warsh could bring along a majority to a hold.

But given Warsh's own repeated declarations that inflation is the Fed's responsibility, the disappointingly hot inflation reading in August, and Trump's recent signal that the war in Iran -- and therefore high oil prices -- may continue for another couple months, he may not want to. 

"We think Waller and Williams will argue in favor of a rate hike on the basis that the 'speed' of the disinflationary process is not satisfactory," EY-Parthenon economist Gregory Daco wrote. "With only one or two dissents favoring a hold, Chairman Warsh will likely use the cover of the majority to lead from behind and also vote for a hike."

(Reporting by Ann Saphir and Michael S. Derby; Editing by Andrea Ricci )

data.title: Adyen Joins Guidewire Marketplace as an Approved Global Payment Partner for Insurers
data.description:
New integration delivers Adyen's single, end-to-end banking infrastructure to Guidewire customers to streamline global insurance payments

NEW YORK, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Adyen, the financial technology platform of choice for leading businesses, today announced that it has been approved as a Global Payment Partner for Guidewire. The integration will be launched through the Guidewire Marketplace, offering property and casualty (P&C) insurers a seamless way to connect Adyen's payment capabilities with their Guidewire core systems.

The launch on the Guidewire Marketplace productizes the significant commercial momentum Adyen has already established within the insurance vertical. By choosing the Adyen integration, insurers can eliminate fragmented regional setups and manage the entire flow of funds throughout the policy lifecycle through a single global platform.

Enhancing the Insurer and Policyholder Experience

The Adyen integration functions as a vetted choice within the Guidewire Marketplace, allowing insurers to optimize front-end payment channels and back-end financial routing. Through this single integration, insurance leaders can seamlessly manage automated premium collections (including cards, ACH, and local payment methods), recurring billing retries, and efficient claims payouts utilizing bank transfers and virtual cards.

Differentiating with Intelligent Money Movement and Existing Market Traction

Unlike traditional payment processors or software-only layers that rely on third-party banks and fragmented regional networks, Adyen operates as a single platform with its own banking licenses. This allows the integration to handle the entire lifecycle of a transaction—from front-end acceptance to back-end clearing and settling—ensuring higher payout speeds, reduced transaction failure, and institutional-grade resilience.

"By launching our exciting integration on the Guidewire Marketplace, we are building upon the strong market leadership in the Insurance market that we've scaled in recent years," said Adrian Davis, Managing Director Financial Services & Insurance at Adyen. "What differentiates Adyen is that we aren't just a software connection; we own the underlying financial infrastructure. As a global platform with our own banking licenses, we manage the full money movement stack end-to-end which ensures Guidewire's customers easily offer whatever payment method their policyholders prefer, effectively turning payments from a legacy hurdle into a strategic advantage for growth."

Advanced Security and Operational Efficiency

Insurers utilizing the marketplace integration will be able to leverage Adyen's full money movement stack across Guidewire's customer base of more than 570 insurers across 43 countries. Key features of the integrated solution include:

  • True End-to-End Processing: Eliminates third-party banking intermediaries, resulting in faster financial routing and reduced operational costs.
  • Unified Reporting: Access to centralized transaction data and automated reconciliation to streamline back-office operations.
  • Built-in Fraud Protection: Utilization of Adyen's machine learning risk engine to identify and mitigate fraudulent insurance activity.
  • Data Security: Advanced tokenization capabilities to keep card-on-file data continuously secure and compliant.

The integration is available globally, allowing insurers across North America, Europe, LATAM, and APAC to leverage the solution after launch in 2027 . Because the integration is standardized for the Guidewire Marketplace, it can be implemented by any Global Systems Integrator (GSI) or an insurer's internal IT team, ensuring maximum flexibility during deployment.

About Adyen

Adyen (AMS: ADYEN) is the financial technology platform of choice for leading companies. By providing end-to-end payments capabilities, data-driven insights, and financial products in a single global solution, Adyen helps businesses achieve their ambitions faster. With offices around the world, Adyen works with the likes of Meta, Uber, H&M, and eBay.

The cooperation with Guidewire as described in this partner update underlines Adyen's continuous growth with current and new partners over the years.

About Guidewire

Guidewire is the platform P&C insurers trust to engage, innovate, and grow efficiently. We combine digital, core, analytics, and AI to deliver our platform as a cloud service. More than 570 insurers in 43 countries, from new ventures to the largest and most complex in the world, run on Guidewire.

data.title: Comcast, Paramount Skydance mull shutting European streaming venture SkyShowtime
data.description:
Sept 14 (Reuters) - Comcast's ( CMCSA ) NBC and Paramount Skydance ( PSKY ) are considering winding down their SkyShowtime joint venture, which streams shows and movies in European markets, according to a letter reviewed by Reuters on Monday.

Here are some details:

* The SkyShowtime board wrote to CEO Monty Sarhan on Monday that it is considering strategic options for the business, including shutting down the platform, amid a competitive and challenging market, according to the letter.

* SkyShowtime, which launched in 2022, is available in 22 European markets, including Spain, Portugal, Denmark and Sweden.

* Sarhan shared the board letter with employees along with his own memo, which was reviewed by Reuters.

* "I know this news creates uncertainty and, as we work through what comes next, my priority and that of the leadership team, is to be there and support all of you," he said in the memo.

* The Hollywood Reporter and Bloomberg News earlier reported the development.

(Reporting by Jaspreet Singh in Bengaluru; Editing by Tasim Zahid)

data.title: Anthropic targets financial advisers with new Claude tool
data.description:
Sept 14 (Reuters) - AI lab Anthropic on Monday launched a set of tools for financial advisers, connecting its Claude chatbot to investment analytics and wealth-management software from firms including BlackRock, Charles Schwab and Addepar. 

The product, called Claude for Financial Advisors, is designed to help financial services firms prepare for client meetings, review portfolios and handle follow-up work.

The launch comes days after rival OpenAI introduced a version of ChatGPT for the industry, targeting investment bankers and equity researchers with tools for financial research, modeling and client materials.

It also builds on Anthropic's broader push into financial services, where it has developed tools based on its AI model Claude for tasks including investment research, portfolio analysis, financial modeling and preparing client materials.

Anthropic's new offering connects Claude with data and software from firms including Envestnet, iCapital, Orion, Wealthbox, Wealth.com and Zocks.

The announcement comes as the pace and cost of AI development faces growing scrutiny, with industry leaders increasingly questioning whether spending can be sustained and how quickly the technology should advance amid mounting fears of misuse.

(Reporting by Harshita Mary Varghese in Bengaluru; Editing by Jonathan Ananda)

data.title: LocalStack Acquires WonderTwin AI to Let Developers and AI Agents Build Integrations Locally
data.description:
ZURICH, Sept. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- LocalStack, the market leader in local cloud development, today announced that it has acquired WonderTwin AI, a provider of local application emulators for AI-native software development workflows including GitHub, HubSpot, PostHog, Stripe and other applications. 

Building and maintaining application integrations requires testing code against live instances of third-party applications via shared sandbox environments that struggle to support the scale and concurrency of AI-native software development workflows. This bottleneck puts more pressure on the software engineering organization to ship reliable applications at the velocity that AI can achieve.

WonderTwin AI emulators simulate third-party applications on local infrastructure so each developer and AI agent can run local sandboxes to test and validate integrations without the implications of connecting to and building against live application APIs. 

LocalStack’s local cloud development platform simulates the behavior of AWS and Snowflake locally so AI-native software engineering organizations can provide a faster, more secure and more effective development experience for agentic AI development workflows responsible for shipping reliable applications to the cloud.

Together, LocalStack and WonderTwin AI will provide AI-native software engineers on-demand, single-tenant sandboxes to validate the entire stack supporting cloud applications without the complexity, delays and risks associated with connecting to live third-party services intended for production workloads.

“As the way engineers build software continues to evolve, our community is discovering gaps in the stack supporting those workflows,” said Waldemar Hummer, co-founder and CTO of LocalStack. “Cloud applications rarely operate in isolation. With WonderTwin AI, we’re extending local development beyond cloud infrastructure to include the third-party APIs and external services applications depend on.”

“The SaaS application testing environment has always been limited. AI agents broke it completely,” said Tela Andrews, founder of WonderTwin AI. “Emulation was the only fix. Joining LocalStack brings full-stack emulation for applications and cloud platforms together under one roof to make concurrent, local validation seamless for any developer and any agent.”

The development experience for full-stack local software development enables engineering teams to ship more reliable applications faster, more efficiently and more securely by removing the need to connect to third-party applications and provision live cloud resources.

With WonderTwin AI and LocalStack:

  • Software developers can quickly spin up local sandboxes to experiment and iterate without waiting for access to shared environments, with the benefits of instant feedback on code updates and improved visibility into failures early in the development process
  • AI agents can maintain integrations and validate cloud behavior without the security and compliance risks of providing AI access to third-party applications or cloud platforms, enabling AI agents to perform validation that previously required human intervention
  • CI/CD pipelines can execute faster tests by instantly testing code against local emulators for applications and cloud platforms, without the delays and costs associated with testing against actual services

About LocalStack
LocalStack’s mission is to make cloud software development easier, faster and more impactful by unlocking the benefits of local infrastructure for cloud-based application environments. With more than 1,500 customers and hundreds of millions of Docker pulls, LocalStack has become the de facto standard for local cloud development worldwide. LocalStack is remote-first and backed by Notable Capital. For more information, please visit https://www.localstack.cloud/.

data.title: Global investment firm Carlyle extends reach in Canada; purchases oil and gas firm Parallax
data.description:
CALGARY, Sept 14 (Reuters) - Global investment firm Carlyle is expanding its reach in Canada through the acquisition of the privately owned Canadian oil and gas company Parallax.

* The acquisition is the second in 12 months by Carlyle's energy group, which last year acquired Kiwetinohk Energy for approximately C$1.4 billion.

* Carlyle has established a newly formed Canadian company called Avenrock Energy, which has reached a deal to acquire Parallax from Carnelian Energy Capital.

* Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed. Sources pegged the total enterprise value of the deal at approximately C$1 billion and said Parallax's gross production is 20,000 boepd.

* Parallax is an established Western Canadian company operating in the East Shale Duvernay in Alberta, with approximately 300,000 acres and a substantial production base focused predominantly on light oil and natural gas liquids.

* Avenrock aims to establish a significant operating presence in Western Canada, with a focus on the continued development of the Parallax asset base to build out a leading Western Canadian light oil platform, according to a release.

(Reporting by Amanda Stephenson in Calgary; Editing by Will Dunham Editing by Nick Zieminski)

data.title: Belfry Software Expands Belle AI Teammate, Launches Belfry Recruiting
data.description:
Belle AI Dispatch and Belle AI Assistant are the two newest jobs handled by Belfry's in-platform AI teammate. Belfry Recruiting is now available as an add-on for all customers.

NEW YORK, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Belfry Software, the all-in-one operating platform built for security guard services companies, today announced two new capabilities for Belle, its in-platform AI teammate, and the launch of Belfry Recruiting, an applicant tracking system now live for Belfry customers.

Belle works inside the Belfry platform as one teammate with distinct jobs. Belle AI Dispatch watches shift exceptions in real time and reaches out to officers. Belle AI Assistant answers operators' questions about their business in plain language.

Security firms run a small back office behind a large field workforce, often eight or more officers per administrative employee. Every new contract adds more routine work: shifts to confirm, clock-ins that never happen, posts that go quiet, open shifts to fill, and data to pull when a client asks.

"The firms we work with aren't short on capability. They're short on time. Belle picks up some of the constant, routine work that used to land on the back office, and Belfry Recruiting brings hiring into the same system as everything else. Both give operators more time for the two things that set them apart: exceptional client service and a great place for officers to work."
-- Jordan Wallach, Co-Founder & CEO, Belfry Software

Belle AI Dispatch Watches Shifts in Real Time

Belle AI Dispatch builds on Belfry's real-time monitoring to help teams resolve urgent issues as they happen. Belle handles first-touch officer outreach on the exceptions that consume dispatcher attention: missed clock-ins, unconfirmed shifts, abandoned posts, early clock-outs, and shifts with no recent activity.

For firms of every size, dispatch keeps client people and property safe, drives client retention, and is expensive to staff at the level needed to cover every exception.

Jason Fellows, founder of Minneapolis-based LincRo Security Solutions, has grown his operation to 120 officers and counting without hiring a back-office dispatcher. Belle has responded to 2,719 missed clock-ins at LincRo, and 2,343 of them, roughly 86 percent, ended with the officer on the clock.

"We can rest easy knowing Belle is watching the schedule for us. We let her do her thing, and if she escalates something to me or my team, that's when we step in and start making calls. Until then, we know she has it covered."
— Jason Fellows, Founder, LincRo Security Solutions

Belfry is also extending Belle AI Dispatch beyond text to reach officers by voice, giving firms a more direct channel for time-critical exceptions. Belle operates under rules the operations team defines and escalates only when it can't resolve an exception on its own. The design goal is triage, not autonomy: routine cases close themselves, and the few that need a human decision arrive clearly flagged.

Belle AI Dispatch is available as a paid add-on to the Belfry platform.

Belle AI Assistant Lets Operators Chat With Their Data

Security firms generate a steady stream of operational data across scheduling, timekeeping, payroll, and billing. Historically, turning that data into an answer meant pulling exports into spreadsheets or waiting on a report someone else had to build.

With Belle AI Assistant, an operator types a question the way they'd ask a colleague and gets an answer built from their own Belfry data. Operators can ask, for example, which sites had the most missed clock-ins last month, where overtime is concentrated this pay period, or which officers have a license or certification expiring in the next 60 days.

Because Belle is built on Belfry's data model for the security industry, it already understands posts, shifts, billable hours, and the other terms operators use, with no setup. Insights that used to take a report request now take a question.

Belfry Recruiting Brings Hiring Into the Same Platform

Belfry Recruiting adds applicant tracking to the platform firms already use to schedule, pay, and manage their officers. Sept 14 (Reuters) - DeepSeek plans to hire Yan Wentao, a partner at venture-capital firm GL Ventures, as its first chief financial officer, two people with knowledge of the matter said, as the Chinese AI startup prepares for a potential initial public offering.

Reuters reported last week that Hangzhou-based DeepSeek had hired Chinese brokerage CITIC Securities to prepare for a possible listing on Shanghai's technology-focused STAR Market.

A CFO typically plays a central role in managing investor communications, financial controls, capital allocation and disclosure processes required for a listing.

The appointment of Yan, who has dealmaking experience, to the role would be a significant step in DeepSeek's transformation from a research-focused lab bankrolled by its founder's hedge fund into a more conventional corporate structure.

The sources on his planned appointment could not be named because they were not authorised to speak publicly on the issue.

GL Ventures is the venture-capital arm of Hillhouse Investment, an investment firm founded by China-born investor Zhang Lei that focuses on sectors including technology, biotech, and consumer industries. Hillhouse is not an investor in DeepSeek.

DeepSeek and Hillhouse did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Yan could not immediately be reached for comment.

Yan was born in 1991, according to Chinese venture-capital publication Zero2IPO, which lists AI developer and DeepSeek rival MiniMax ( MNMXF ) among his representative investments.

DEEPSEEK RAISES CAPITAL AND INVESTS IN TALENT

As the global race to dominate AI accelerates, DeepSeek is in an ongoing fundraising round that values it at about 500 billion yuan ($74 billion), Reuters reported in July. 

In June, it raised about $7.4 billion at a post-money valuation of more than $50 billion. 

It has also increased spending on computing infrastructure, chip development, and talent.

Early last year, the company made global headlines when it released low-cost AI models that led to investor scepticism about U.S. claims on the massive spending needed to build advanced AI systems.

It is controlled by founder Liang, who financed the startup via his quantitative hedge fund High-Flyer from its inception in 2023 until earlier this year, when it began seeking external fundraising.

data.title: Analysis-Winter is coming: airBaltic debt woes herald tough season ahead for smaller airlines
data.description:
LONDON, Sept 14 (Reuters) - After Latvian airline airBaltic filed Chapter 11 proceedings on Monday, the aviation sector is bracing for a tough winter as the Iran war continues to push up jet fuel costs.

The U.S. war with Iran has sparked the worst airline crisis in terms of costs since the COVID-19 pandemic, and airBaltic became the first European carrier during the conflict to file for bankruptcy, while U.S. peer Spirit collapsed in May after seeking protection before the war.

Airlines operate with relatively thin margins compared to other sectors, leaving them more exposed to geopolitical turmoil, particularly in winter when they burn through cash they earned in the busy summer season as bookings and travel slow.

SACRIFICING RETURNS

Smaller carriers are particularly vulnerable to further earnings pressure, with the price of jet fuel set to stay high as long as the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked.

"Smaller, niche players are (most) at risk," aviation analyst John Strickland said.

Bigger budget airlines that depend on offering cheap fares are also being hit hard by a doubling of fuel prices since the war began in late February, although they also have individual strengths.

Wizz Air's ( WZZAF ) operating losses deepened in the first quarter, it reported last month, saying it expects revenue per seat to keep falling in the current quarter after it cut fares to attract passengers. They reached a record 8.7 million in August.

"Supported by strong liquidity, a disciplined hedging programme and one of Europe's youngest and most efficient fleets, Wizz Air ( WZZAF ) continues to invest, grow and serve more customers than ever," the airline said in a statement to Reuters on Monday.

James Halstead, managing partner at Aviation Strategy, said that Wizz Air ( WZZAF ) is in a better position than state-owned airlines thanks to its stock market listing.

"They are growing strongly, which means they are sacrificing returns now for future stability. They have a very good brand and operating model and they do have support," he said.

Elsewhere, Southeast Asian budget carrier AirAsia is seeking to raise fresh capital after consistent losses and an aggressive restructuring, while Canada's Air Transat has struggled with spiralling jet fuel costs.

AirAsia said it saw no problems with its business sustainability and was seeing strong underlying demand.

"AirAsia remains focused on maintaining business continuity and stable operations across all its markets and we continue to see strong underlying demand across our network," AirAsia said in a statement. "We are also working closely with our stakeholders to manage our financial and operational requirements."

Air Transat did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

MORE ROUTES FOR BIGGER PLAYERS

A tough market could see some smaller national airlines cede routes to larger, deeper-pocketed rivals, executives and investors said. They could also face challenges from budget airlines such as Ryanair and Wizz Air ( WZZAF ) that have taken over smaller secondary airports and worked to take plum slots and routes across central Europe in a push for growth - offering consumers better price options, analysts say.

In August, Wizz Air ( WZZAF ) CEO Jozsef Varadi told reporters that the carrier was keen to take over routes from Romania's state-backed carrier TAROM.

TAROM did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

The tougher market conditions could accelerate a long-standing move in Europe towards consolidation, pushing some smaller carriers into bigger groups like British Airways-owner IAG, Lufthansa and Air France-KLM.

Norse Atlantic ( NRSAF ), which is still reporting quarterly losses, in July started a process for a sale or merger. It did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Poland's state-owned carrier LOT has been a suspected consolidation target for years. LOT did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

AirBaltic has said it is looking for another strategic investor, but none has publicly expressed interest to date.

Lufthansa owns a 10% stake in airBaltic but has said it doesn't plan to increase its stake. It declined to comment on what its next steps could be given airBaltic's Chapter 11 proceedings.

Still, analysts said Chapter 11 proceedings could give airBaltic the chance to recover and survive, unlike Spirit.

"This gives them a protective framework to put their house in order," said Strickland, pointing to Scandinavian rival SAS as a successful example of a turnaround.

(Reporting by Joanna Plucinska and Gianluca Lo Nostro; Editing by Adam Jourdan and Susan Fenton)

data.title: King Charles to host AI executives as threat fears mount
data.description:
LONDON, Sept 14 (Reuters) - Britain's King Charles will host the leaders of major artificial intelligence companies this week to discuss whether a shared set of principles is needed to guide a technology that has sparked growing warnings about its threat to humanity.

With the biggest names in AI calling for a slowdown in its development, Charles will host executives from Nvidia ( NVDA ), Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Anthropic, and the UK minister for AI, to discuss how the technology can be harnessed to benefit society and uphold human dignity.

The debate about AI was thrust back into the spotlight when two Anthropic researchers issued warnings that the rapidly progressing technology could lead to the extinction of the human race ‌in the not-too-distant future. 

The chief executive of Anthropic, Dario Amodei, said on Saturday that companies must slow the pace of advance of AI models.

Attendees at the king's summit will include Nvidia ( NVDA ) founder and chief executive Jensen Huang, Google DeepMind founder and chairman Demis Hassabis and Paolo Benanti, an adviser to the Vatican on AI, according to the Sunday Times.

Britain's Minister for Artificial Intelligence Kanishka Narayan will also attend.

San Francisco-based Anthropic released a threat intelligence report last week detailing how several actors had used its Claude AI models for activities ranging from weapons development and cyber operations to surveillance and fraud.

However, securing a global stance will be difficult: U.S. President Donald Trump rejected any talk of a slowdown on Sunday while China's Global Times tabloid said it was really a "Cold War playbook" targeting Beijing.      

Charles, both as king and when he was the Prince of Wales, has used his position to convene meetings to discuss a range of topics, most notably on the environment. 

Buckingham Palace said the gathering would discuss how AI could be harnessed in ways that benefit society and contribute "to the flourishing of both people and the planet".

Britain, the European leader in AI funding ⁠and startups, has favoured a ‌light-touch approach to AI regulation, aligning more closely with the United States than the European Union.

Britain's AI Security Institute, established after the AI Safety Summit in 2023, receives pre-deployment access to AI models under voluntary ​agreements with the major AI companies, enabling it to ​assess their capabilities and risks, and giving it a window into frontier AI development. 

(Reporting by Kate Holton, additional reporting by Michael Holden and Paul Sandle, editing by Andrew Cawthorne)

data.title: US STOCKS-Wall St falls as AI anxiety batters Nvidia, chipmakers

* Indexes down: Dow 0.23%, S&P 500 0.42%, Nasdaq 0.44%

* Chipmakers fall, while software stocks climb

* AI heavyweights push for model development slowdown

(Updates with late morning trading)

By Niket Nishant and Tharuniyaa Lakshmi

Sept 14 (Reuters) - Wall Street's main indexes fell on Monday, pummeled by a selloff in heavyweight AI stocks after top U.S. executives raised safety concerns and called for slowing the development of artificial-intelligence capabilities.

Shares of Nvidia ( NVDA ) tumbled 3%, hitting their lowest level in nearly three weeks, while "Magnificent Seven" peer Amazon ( AMZN ) shed more than 1%.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Saturday called on artificial intelligence companies to slow the pace at which they advance model capabilities. Elon Musk, who runs xAI, and ​OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said they agreed with Amodei.

The losses reflect waning exuberance as the frenzied race to develop increasingly capable AI models gives way to a clear-eyed reassessment.

Billions of dollars poured into AI have powered a stratospheric rise in some technology and semiconductor stocks and were critical to strong equity market gains over the past few years.

"Three rivals now agree that the fastest engine in technology needs a governor. The market still has to learn how hard that governor will press," said Matthew Tuttle, CEO of Tuttle Capital Management.

At 11:40 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 123.22 points, or 0.23%, to 52,450.07, the S&P 500 lost 32.20 points, or 0.42%, to 7,624.78, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 114.87 points, or 0.44%, to trade at 26,218.17.

The declines narrowed from earlier in the session, after U.S. President Donald Trump said Iran wants to make a deal and that he would decide whether the United States would engage in the effort.

Chipmakers declined, with Intel ( INTC ), AMD and Marvell Technology ( MRVL ) down 5%, 5% and 6%, respectively.

The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index fell about 5% and was on track for its worst daily drop since July, if current losses hold.

Eight of the 11 major S&P 500 indexes traded lower, with industrials and technology leading declines.

Consumer staples and healthcare rose about 2% and 1%, respectively, as investors sought shelter in defensive areas of the market.

Shares of software stocks, which have been dampened by concerns AI could disrupt their businesses, climbed. ServiceNow ( NOW ) , Adobe and Workday were up 7%, 4% and 5%, respectively.

Meta and Alphabet climbed around 2% each.

TRADERS EXPECT FED RATE INCREASE

Concerns about the potential harms of AI intensified when Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned last week and said the "people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade."

The weakness in equities could set the tone for markets ahead of a potential interest-rate hike later in the week, with traders pricing in a nearly 90% chance of a rate increase by the U.S. Federal Reserve, according to CME's FedWatch.

Oil prices are also trading close to levels not seen since May. Brent crude futures advanced about 4% to $108.52, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures rose more than 3% to $103.81.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.75-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 1.14-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.

The S&P 500 posted nine new 52-week highs and eight new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 34 new highs and 152 new lows.

data.title: US personal injury law firm Morgan & Morgan touts $1 billion AI investment, plans to sell platform to other firms
data.description:
Sept 14 (Reuters) - Morgan & Morgan, which bills itself as the largest U.S. personal injury law firm, said on Monday that it has committed to investing at least $1 billion into AI and technology over the next decade and will begin marketing its own AI platform to other law firms next year.

The Orlando, Florida-based firm said it already spent $300 million building its AI platform, called MX2, which it said it uses to extract medical information, generate case documents and prepare for trials. It said the platform now has nearly 5,000 monthly users.

The investment will include hiring personnel and building new software and security capabilities, Yath Ithayakumar, the firm's chief transformation officer, said in an interview. The majority "is going to be very targeted towards AI," he said.

The announcement comes as major corporate defense law firms are also investing heavily in AI. Kirkland & Ellis said in May that it is devoting $500 million of its revenue to developing a custom AI platform over the next three to four years.

Other law firms have inked agreements with major technology companies to jointly create AI tools. London-based Freshfields said in April it will work with the legal team at Anthropic, the maker of Claude, to develop AI applications for legal services. Reuters' parent company Thomson Reuters also sells AI-assisted tools for ​the legal industry.

Morgan & Morgan founder John Morgan said in a statement that his firm, with more than 1,100 lawyers, was ahead of its rivals in AI adoption and that trial-focused firms like his were more insulated than corporate firms from being replaced by the technology.

"Firms which bill by the hour to draft and review agreements or read through thousands of pages of documents are the practices AI will replace - almost entirely," he said.

The firm said it plans to make MX2 available to other law firms, including corporate and transactional practices, by the end of 2027 on an invitation-only basis.

"We think we're in a great position to help law firms solve tough problems and we're confident we can do it," Ithayakumar said. The firm did not say how it would price access to the platform.

Reuters had reported in June that Morgan & Morgan, which has annual revenue of $2.4 billion, had hired JPMorgan ( JPM ) to explore a minority stake sale that could eventually make way for the firm to go public.

Widespread AI adoption by lawyers is expected to speed their work, but it has also created problems when attorneys have relied on AI-generated results without checking their accuracy. A federal judge in Wyoming sanctioned two lawyers from Morgan & Morgan last year for citing fake cases generated by AI in a court filing.

Ithayakumar said the error in the case took place "because we were early adopters of AI and we were moving fast." He said the firm has invested in training processes to make it easier for lawyers and staff to review AI outputs.

(Reporting by Sara Merken in New York)

data.title: US lacks funding to complete first phase of air traffic control reforms, report finds
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Sept 14 (Reuters) - The Federal Aviation Administration needs more funding from Congress to complete phase one of a $10.6 billion air traffic control reform plan and has underestimated the total costs of operating the new system, according to a government report released on Monday.

The Government Accountability Office said the FAA had not fully assessed the costs of operating the new system or set a detailed schedule for completing reforms.

"In essence, the FAA is buying delivery speed at the risk of cost uncertainty and potential disruptions," the GAO report said, adding, "these risks increase the likelihood of FAA repeating its history of cost overruns, delays, and unmet performance targets."

Congress previously approved $9 billion for ATC reforms in the first phase. The FAA is also using $1 billion from its current-year budget and needs another $574 million, the GAO said. The price tag for telecommunications upgrades has jumped $4.75 billion to $5.91 billion, GAO said.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford is set to testify on Tuesday before Congress on the effort and its plan to begin deploying a software-based program to try to avoid flight delays.

The GAO said the FAA has over 11,000 separate projects in phase one of the $10.6 billion reform plan.

The FAA said in a letter to the GAO that it is committed to using best practices to oversee the project that it says "remains largely on plan," including over 95% of specific tasks.

The FAA's existing air traffic control systems are "severely outdated, underperforming, and unsustainable. This aging and unreliable technology has contributed to an increase in aviation incidents," GAO said.

Replacing air traffic control tower voice switches carries the highest risk because of the size of the sites and airspace it controls, the age of technology and need to operate new and old voice switches simultaneously.

The GAO noted that the FAA released its first comprehensive plan for improving air traffic control services in 1982 and has since suffered a series of cost overruns and delays while delivering limited results.

The FAA in December tapped Peraton, which is owned by Veritas Capital, to oversee the modernization effort, awarding it a $1.5 billion contract.

(Reporting by David Shepardson Editing by Nick Zieminski and Bill Berkrot)

data.title: Open Secure AI Alliance Joins the Linux Foundation to Build a Shared, Open Defense Stack for the AI Era
data.description:
Originally founded by dozens of enterprise leaders and NVIDIA, the Alliance moves to neutral governance to expand industry collaboration on open AI security tools, research and shared defenses

SAN FRANCISCO, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Linux Foundation, the world's leading home for collaboration on open source software, hardware, standards and data today announced that the Open Secure AI Alliance has joined the Linux Foundation, establishing a neutral home for organizations across AI, cybersecurity and open source to build and share an open defensive stack for securing software and AI agents.

As organizations build AI into software and infrastructure, effective defenses must extend across models and inference, agents and context, identity and policy, enforcement, containment and the underlying infrastructure. Originally established by NVIDIA in collaboration with members including the Linux Foundation, the Open Secure AI Alliance develops open technologies that give security leaders the ability to inspect how those defenses work, adapt them to their environments, run them on infrastructure they control, and build greater resilience as models, vendors and infrastructure evolve.

"AI systems should be secure, reliable and predictable," said Jim Zemlin, CEO of the Linux Foundation. "By bringing the Open Secure AI Alliance to the Linux Foundation, we are creating a neutral home where industry, researchers and governments can collaborate on open tools, shared standards and evidence-based practices that strengthen security and support AI innovation."

"AI security improves when organizations openly share what they learn," said Justin Boitano, vice president, Enterprise AI, NVIDIA. "With the Linux Foundation as its new home, the Open Secure AI Alliance can bring together experts across models, harnesses and infrastructure to turn shared evidence into practical, verifiable defenses for the entire AI stack."

The Alliance is focused on two complementary goals: building an open defensive stack for AI and strengthening collective defense by enabling organizations to test systems, share evidence and turn discoveries into protections that can benefit the broader ecosystem. These contributions run alongside existing Linux Foundation security communities, including the Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF), creating opportunities to advance shared standards and defensive infrastructure across open source software and AI.

Shared AI Findings Exchange - Request for Comments

A core initiative within the Alliance is the Shared AI Findings Exchange (SAFE), an effort designed to help organizations learn collectively from AI security incidents. SAFE is intended to confidentially collect and analyze findings, promptly inform affected parties and convert recurring failures into evidence-based controls that organizations can use to strengthen their defenses. Developers, defenders, researchers and organizations are invited to contribute to the SAFE proposal by September 21, after which the Alliance will work with its members to integrate feedback and move the guidelines forward.

Why Collective Defense Matters

The Alliance ensures no single vendor controls the end-to-end AI stack by helping enterprises move agentic AI from experimentation into production, including best practices such as:

  • Keeping the AI stack open across models, agent harnesses, datasets, prompts, reference architectures and evaluations so defenders can adapt protections to their environments.
  • Applying proven security fundamentals to AI agents: asset visibility, identity and permissions, deterministic controls, change management, monitoring and clear human accountability.
  • Developing shared evaluation standards, stronger attribution and rapid, trusted sharing of agent traces and incident lessons so the community can turn incidents into practical controls.
  • Exercising test response playbooks and tabletop simulations to prepare before incidents occur and scale AI adoption with greater confidence.

NVIDIA will join the Linux Foundation community at Open Source Summit Europe in Prague, CZ on October 7 to talk about building collective defense in the AI era. Register here to join the event before standard rates end on September 21.

To learn more about the Open Secure AI Alliance and how to participate, visit https://secureaialliance.org/.

About the Linux Foundation
The Linux Foundation is the world's leading home for collaboration on open source software, hardware, standards and data. Linux Foundation projects, including Linux, Kubernetes, Model Context Protocol (MCP), OpenChain, OpenSearch, OpenSSF, OpenStack, PyTorch, Ray, RISC-V, SPDX and Zephyr, provide the foundation for global infrastructure. The Linux Foundation is focused on leveraging best practices and addressing the needs of contributors, users, and solution providers to create sustainable models for open collaboration. data.title: GENFIT Advances Nangibotide in Phase 2 Clinical Investigation in ACLF
data.description:

  • The investigation in Phase 2 is supported by a robust scientific and clinical foundation around the TREM-1 pathway and the asset's profile:

    • Multiple efficacy signals already observed with nangibotide across three Phase 2 clinical trials in septic shock and COVID-19 subjects, including a statistically significant reduction in mortality in severe COVID-19 and significant improvements in SOFA score from baseline in septic shock

Lille (France), Cambridge (Massachusetts, United States), September 14, 2026 - GENFIT , a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to improving the lives of patients with rare and life-threatening liver diseases, today announced the strengthening of its pipeline through the acquisition of nangibotide in summer 2026, and its plan to investigate nangibotide in a Phase 2 clinical trial for the treatment of Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure (ACLF).

A clinical and regulatory foundation supporting rapid development
Nangibotide has an extensive human safety package, built on experience from more than 400 subjects across acute inflammatory conditions, supporting the program to move directly into proof-of-concept evaluation in ACLF.

In the post-hoc analysis of Phase 2 clinical trials conducted in septic shock and COVID-19, nangibotide demonstrated multiple efficacy signals, including a statistically significant reduction in mortality.

The existing regulatory and CMC (Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls) packages for nangibotide are also well advanced to support rapid clinical development in ACLF, allowing the program to build on an extensive clinical safety database and a mature, well-established manufacturing platform.

data.title: Global AI stocks fall as industry chiefs call for slowing development
data.description:
By Johann M Cherian and Gregor Stuart Hunter

Sept 14 (Reuters) - AI-linked stocks plunged worldwide on Monday after leaders of the biggest artificial intelligence companies warned of risks from rapid development, the starkest threat yet to the billions of dollars being poured into the industry that have driven world markets to record highs.

The selloff rippled through the industry, where companies are increasingly relying on debt and circular financing to fund ambitious AI spending plans even as global borrowing costs, reflected in multi-year-high bond yields, continue to rise.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, in a lengthy essay shared on X on Saturday, called on AI companies to slow the rate at which they advance model capabilities amid mounting fears of misuse of artificial intelligence. Both Elon Musk, who runs xAI, and Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, said they agree with Amodei.

Altman also said the company would not proceed with an IPO this year, citing safety concerns.

Wall Street's elite tech index, the Nasdaq 100, slid 1.2% to a six-week low in early trading as chip stocks, which have led the AI sugar rush, fell the most.

"If this does lead to sort of a slowdown and a rethink of AI spending, that will have ramifications for the economy and some important sectors of the stock market, because essentially, we've been running hot based on AI spending," said Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers.

The Philadelphia chip index dropped 5.1%, with Nvidia down 3.6%, Advanced Micro Devices off 5.6% and Micron falling 6%, while Musk's SpaceX shed 1.6%.

Semiconductor equipment makers Lam Research and Applied Materials tumbled 6% each, while tech utilities Bloom Energy lost 6.8% and GE Vernova declined 7.4%.

Europe's tech sector fell 2.2%, dragged by ASML's 5.9% decline, alongside steep losses in Infineon and Siemens Energy, while in Asia, SoftBank plunged as much as 13.2% and chipmakers TSMC and SK Hynix ( SKHY ) also retreated.

"UNACCEPTABLE" RISKS

Alarm about the potential harm from AI spiked earlier this month when Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned, stating that the "people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade."

A few days later, the San Francisco-based AI lab released a threat intelligence report detailing how its Claude AI models were used for activities ranging from weapons development and cyber operations to surveillance and fraud.

Over the weekend, Amodei wrote that in six to 12 months, AI agents "could be capable of taking over the entire internet potentially causing hundreds of billions of dollars in damage." Separately, OpenAI's Altman said in an interview that risks of human extinction posed by AI were "unacceptable".

And while several U.S. lawmakers have raised concern about AI's rapid progress and called for new rules, U.S. President Donald Trump said that a "sick conspiracy" against AI and data centres exists, appearing to play down concerns expressed by industry leaders.

AI-related trades have powered much of the gains in global equities since OpenAI released ChatGPT in 2022, but more recently cyberattacks by rogue AI agents and public discontent with data centre construction have raised opposition to the development of the industry.

The U.S. and Chinese governments are expected to hold AI safety talks as part of bilateral discussions taking place this month, Reuters reported. But China's state-backed Global Times blasted the Anthropic essay in an editorial, calling it a "Cold War playbook" intended to curb the country's technological development.

A growing concern for OpenAI and Anthropic is the rising competition from more affordable Chinese models such as Moonshot AI's Kimi K3, Alibaba's Qwen and DeepSeek's offerings, which could pressure the pricing of larger, more costly models.

NOT ALL BELIEVE THE WARNINGS

Some investors dismissed the warnings from Anthropic and OpenAI.

Michael Burry, whose prescient bets against the U.S. housing market before the 2008 financial crisis were chronicled in the movie "The Big Short", said in a message on X the warnings were "hype and puffery" and "cover for real uncontrollable slowing growth".

Others have argued that record capital spending commitments suggest AI development is unlikely to slow, such as Morgan Stanley's CEO, Ted Pick, who forecast earlier this year that AI spending will surpass $1.3 trillion by 2027.

"The key question is whether this is the first sign that the extraordinary AI investment cycle might eventually moderate. For now, that seems unlikely. The competitive race between companies and countries remains intense, and it's difficult to imagine firms voluntarily stepping back while rivals continue to push ahead," Deutsche Bank said in a note.

Meanwhile, Amodei's Anthropic has pushed ahead with its public debut, expected next month as sources told Reuters that the company is in talks to bring in Nvidia as an anchor investor.

Japanese chipmaker Kioxia Holdings ( KXHCF ) is also considering raising at least $10 billion by listing American depositary receipts, a report said.

(Reporting by Gregor Stuart Hunter in Singapore, Johann M Cherian, Purvi Agarwal and Utkarsh Tushar Hathi in Bengaluru; Additional reporting by Rocky Swift in Tokyo; Editing by Muralikumar Anantharaman and Saumyadeb Chakrabarty)

data.title: Akuity Launches Agentic Control Plane for Software Delivery, Bringing Operational Context and Governance to AI Agents
data.description:
SUNNYVALE, Calif., Sept. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Akuity, the provider of the software delivery platform built by the creators of Argo CD and Kargo, today introduced its Agentic Control Plane and MCP Server. Akuity's Agentic Control Plane lets AI agents accelerate software delivery by giving them the operational context and permissions to act, all governed by the same controls Akuity already enforces across the pipeline. That governance is what gives engineering leadership the confidence to let agents into production, with real control over what agents can touch.

Agentic engineering is driving teams to write more code than ever but shipping it safely has become the bottleneck. Agents are operating inside production environments, sanctioned or not, often with limited access to the data they would need to make a real impact. Many also connect through open-source MCP servers that grant raw access with no identity inheritance, no policy layer and no agent-aware audit trail, expanding the attack surface with every new connection.

“Within hours of enabling Akuity's Agentic Control Plane, it identified more than one hundred degraded applications, and in under ten minutes, it flagged one project as the source of a systemic issue, traced it to the root cause and had a fix ready to go. That's exactly the workflow we wanted: identify the problem, tell us if it's systemic and hand us the fix. This is already bringing value to the team, and we are looking to expand its adoption,” said Michael Goodness, Principal DevOps Engineer, MLB.

"AI agents have moved past writing code to operating how infrastructure changes get delivered and promoted to production, whether we've built the guardrails for it or not. The winners in this next phase won't be whoever adopts AI fastest, it'll be whoever gives their agents a safe, reliable path to do that work. That's what Akuity’s Agentic Control Plane is for," said Hong Wang, co-founder and CEO of Akuity. 

Akuity's Agentic Control Plane is different from point solutions that have added guardrails or generic AI gateways that broker access to them: it runs the software delivery pipeline itself, capturing the deployment history, cluster health and change lineage that these other solutions don't have access to. That operational data is what lets agents move beyond writing code to actually shipping it.

Akuity MCP Server allows AI agents, in-house or third-party such as Claude, Codex or Cursor, to access the Akuity Platform, from cluster health down to the exact commit behind every deployment. Every request they make routes through the Agentic Control Plane which authenticates it as the specific user who connected the agent.

Akuity's Agentic Control Plane features include:

  • Full operational context, not just application data. Point solutions and generic AI gateways give agents visibility into the deployment pipeline but nothing beneath it. Akuity's context extends to the infrastructure it runs on, cluster health and change lineage across the entire fleet so an agent can troubleshoot real incidents, not just the release it just shipped.
  • Guardrails engineering leadership can trust. Every agent action runs through the same identity, permissions and audit trail. A policy layer restricts what agents can touch, including sensitive production actions a team may not want to delegate even when the underlying user has access.
  • One connection, no new liabilities. A single connection authenticates once and carries the user's existing permissions across every instance and cluster it manages. There are no separate credentials to provision or rotate and no new endpoint for security to worry about.

With Akuity's Agentic Control Plane, customers can:

  • Gain visibility without the overhead. Users can ask a single question and get an answer across every cluster instead of checking each one separately.
  • Stand up new services in hours, not weeks. Users can start from an empty repo and ask their agent to bootstrap the entire delivery setup for a new service, environments, promotion rules and all and ship it the same afternoon.
  • Promote a release without leaving the chat. Users can ask their agent to check a release's promotion history and eligibility then promote it to the next environment. Existing approval rules still apply whether a person or an agent made the request.
  • Agent-to-agent troubleshooting. Users can ask their agent to troubleshoot a struggling instance. Their agent connects directly to Akuity's On-Call Agent, pulling in logs and recent changes to diagnose the issue and recommend a fix.

About Akuity 
Akuity is the provider of the leading software delivery platform for enterprise-ready delivery, continuous promotion and AI-powered intelligence for industry leaders. Akuity was founded by the original creators of Argo CD and Kargo; the team has experience running tens of thousands of applications at scale with multi-billion dollar impact. Akuity is based in Sunnyvale, CA. For more information, go to: https://akuity.io/.

data.title: Waymo to bring autonomous ride-hailing to Las Vegas
data.description:
Sept 14 (Reuters) - Alphabet's self-driving unit Waymo said on Monday it will offer rides to the general public in Las Vegas, marking its first foray into Nevada, as it expands its robotaxi service in more U.S. states.

Waymo, which was valued at $126 billion in February when it raised $16 billion, has been growing its robotaxi fleet as it competes with Amazon's ( AMZN ) Zoox and Tesla in the self-driving vehicle market.

Here are more details:

* Waymo will invite public riders to use its services in Las Vegas as it starts off with a few dozen vehicles, with plans to scale over time.

data.title: Analysis-Bitcoin's late summer rally set to face off against the Fed, Congress
data.description:
Sept 14 (Reuters) - Bitcoin bulls are back after months of gloom, but a Federal Reserve rate decision this week will test that optimism, even as a key Senate vote on crypto legislation could provide a surprise tailwind.

After languishing for months at two-year lows of around $60,000, the world's largest cryptocurrency in late August staged a rebound past $70,000 as surging Treasury yields briefly retreated and broader sentiment improved. The rally marked a sharp turnaround for bitcoin, which had slumped roughly 50% from its October 2025 peak of above $126,000.

Although traders are assigning almost no chance of bitcoin rescaling that peak, the bitcoin options market has flipped bullish for the first time in 12 months, according to data from options platform Derive.xyz, with many traders betting bitcoin could hit $80,000 or higher by December.

At first glance, that optimism seems misguided: tensions in the Middle East remain high, the odds of the U.S. Senate passing a key crypto bill that could boost adoption have dimmed, and inflation has remained elevated, raising expectations of a Fed rate hike which usually sucks liquidity out of such risk assets.

Despite those headwinds, many investors believe bitcoin, a notoriously volatile asset, has hit its lowest ebb. With traders assigning an 85% likelihood of a rate hike on Wednesday following hot inflation data, and with long-end bond yields nearing 5%, creating more competition for capital, the question now is whether bitcoin can sustain momentum, said analysts.

"BTC was in oversold territory for some time," said Matthew Dibb, chief operating officer of Singapore-based crypto investment manager Stack Funds. "Short-term traders are looking towards inflation figures and rate rises as short term threats."

OPTIONS TRADERS SKEW BULLISH

The 25-delta skew, which compares demand for bullish call options against protective put options, turned positive on August 20, said Sean Dawson, head of research at Derive.xyz. That implies there is a premium to buying upside calls, he said.

"That is a bit bullish," he added. Dawson attributed the improved mood to a general rotation back into crypto after the blockbuster SpaceX IPO sucked capital out of the market, while Korean equities, also attractive to speculative investors, have cooled.

Open interest for the December 25 expiry is clustered at the $80,000 strike, with about $710 million in notional value, and at $100,000, with roughly $530 million, according to Derive.xyz.

Bitcoin exchange-traded funds, which have institutional as well as retail investors, have also shown signs of renewed demand, with inflows reaching nearly $2 billion the week of August 17, after eight straight weeks of outflows in May and June.

"People in crypto here are actually kind of now looking through all the bad and saying, 'Well, what's the upside?'" said Jim Ferraioli, head of crypto research at Charles Schwab.

An indication from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh that a rate hike would be a one-off rather than the start of a hiking cycle could be one such upside surprise, Ferraioli said. Warsh has so far resisted committing the Fed to any set rate path, analysts said.

Still, it is unlikely that a hike of any kind would be immediately seen as a positive for bitcoin and other speculative assets, said Joseph Edwards, an independent financial researcher. "It would likely put a damper on the recent rally."

While rising Treasury yields are typically a headwind for risk assets, some bitcoin bulls argue that the Treasury's increased buybacks, which investors see as a bid to tamp down yields, could stoke concerns about dollar debasement. That would in turn boost demand for scarce assets such as bitcoin.

"We think bitcoin's structural demand picture is improving, even as the near-term setup has become more vulnerable to macro and positioning-related volatility. The debasement trade appears to be returning," said Brian Vieten, senior analyst at brokerage and wealth management firm Siebert Financial.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION CRYPTO POLICY IN FOCUS

Under President Donald Trump's crypto-friendly administration, policy surprises offer another potential bitcoin boost.

The market has likely priced in that the U.S. Clarity Act, a key crypto bill, will not pass amid delays and continued opposition from many senators, said Can-Luca Köymen, investment strategist at Switzerland-based digital asset bank Sygnum.

The bill would address what the industry says is legal ambiguity by defining which tokens qualify as securities versus commodities, potentially boosting adoption. The U.S. Senate is set to take a procedural vote on the bill on Tuesday, which could ultimately determine its fate.

"If the bill unexpectedly passes, I think that would be a fundamental catalyst to the upside," said Ferraioli.

The technology reaches clients as a Forge Squad: teams made up of human engineers, Digital Twins and a Forge FDE, AI/R's AI Forward Deployed Engineer who orchestrates the work between them.

“Today, the rarest expertise on the market is no longer that of the person who writes code—it's that of the person who understands both code and an industry at the same time. Coding assistants speed up code writing, but they don't carry the rules, standards and constraints of a specific sector. TwinForge preserves that expertise in a platform and makes it possible to apply it at scale, with a human in charge and under the same governance the organization already uses for its other AI initiatives,” says Alisson Aguiar, CTO of Business Apps at AI/R.

In a recent project, after adopting the platform, one squad went from 68 to 150 pull requests per week within a month. In six weeks, Digital Twins already accounted for 72% of the approved volume in the workflow analyzed.

How a Digital Twin is forged and directed

TwinForge is designed to expand the capacity of engineering teams with specialized agents that are supervised and integrated into the processes already in place. The platform combines automation, human validation and governance so companies can adopt AI in software development without giving up control, security or traceability.

Each Digital Twin reproduces the technical repertoire and industry knowledge associated with a specific role, such as architecture, quality, backend engineering and even engineering for specific platforms like Salesforce, Adobe and Shopify. Digital Twins are orchestrated by Forge FDEs, AI/R's AI Forward Deployed Engineers who join the client's team. The Twins open pull requests, but the decision to merge remains subject to review by the engineer responsible. With each cycle, based on what is approved and what is rejected, the Twins take on a larger share of the workflow.

That group—human engineers, Digital Twins and a Forge FDE in charge—is the Forge Squad, the format in which TwinForge already operates inside client development teams.

An extension of the AI/Cockpit ecosystem

TwinForge was built on top of AI/Cockpit—AI/R's software development platform—drawing on its technology foundation, integration capabilities and layers of governance, security and agent management. data.title: Sentinel Water Solutions Marks One Year of PFAS Treatment and More Than 200 Million Gallons Treated at Perkasie Regional Authority
data.description:
Temporary GAC system provided early compliance while creating a pathway to reuse carbon in the Authority’s permanent treatment facility

PERKASIE, Pa.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Sentinel Water Solutions (Sentinel) and Perkasie Regional Authority are celebrating one year of successful operation of the Authority’s temporary granular activated carbon (GAC) treatment system, which has now treated more than 200 million gallons of drinking water while the Authority advances construction of its permanent PFAS treatment facilities.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260914217175/en/

The temporary system was deployed in 2025 as an interim solution that allowed the Authority to begin PFAS treatment a year ahead of the completion of its first permanent facility. Sentinel provided four DESOTEC Mobicon vessels pre-loaded with approximately 10,000 pounds of NSF-certified GAC each, along with an automated booster pump skid and pressure-control improvements to integrate the rental equipment with the Authority’s existing infrastructure.

Perkasie elected to move forward with temporary treatment in parallel with the larger capital project, rather than waiting for construction of the permanent plant to be completed. The approach allowed the Authority to pull its PFAS compliance schedule forward, providing treatment to customers while permanent improvements were still being designed and constructed. The original project was specifically developed around this parallel approach to accelerate compliance and safe water delivery.

After a full year of operation and more than 200 million gallons treated, the project is also demonstrating how temporary treatment can be incorporated into a utility’s long-term treatment strategy rather than viewed as a disposable interim investment.

The GAC currently operating in the rental system is planned to become the foundation of Perkasie’s GAC reactivation pool. As carbon is removed from service, it can be reactivated for future use, creating an inventory of Authority-owned reactivated GAC that can ultimately be deployed in the permanent PFAS treatment facility. The strategy allows Perkasie to carry value from the temporary system forward into its permanent treatment program while reducing reliance on virgin carbon and supporting a more sustainable lifecycle approach to PFAS treatment.

“What makes this project exciting is that the temporary system wasn’t simply a bridge until the permanent plant was completed,” said Andrew Strassner, President of Sentinel Water Solutions. “Now the carbon that helped expedite compliance can become part of the Authority’s long-term reactivation program. It’s a great example of how utilities can address an immediate compliance need without losing sight of the long-term operating strategy.”

The approach builds on Sentinel’s partnership with DESOTEC to provide NSF-certified GAC reactivation and carbon inventory management. The original installation was designed from the outset with future reactivation in mind.

For utilities facing similar PFAS compliance schedules, the Perkasie project demonstrates an alternative to waiting for a permanent capital project to move through design, permitting and construction. Rapidly deployable rental treatment can provide an interim path to compliance, while thoughtful media planning can ensure that investments made during the temporary treatment period continue to provide value after the permanent facility comes online.

“Perkasie’s proactive approach a year ago allowed treatment to begin a year ahead of schedule,” Strassner added. “Reaching 200 million gallons is an important milestone, but the bigger success is that the interim solution is becoming part of the permanent solution.”

Sentinel Water Solutions provides PFAS and emerging contaminant treatment solutions for drinking water utilities, including pilot testing, treatment equipment, rental systems, GAC and ion exchange media services, vessel exchanges, and NSF-certified GAC reactivation. Sentinel focuses on providing practical, rapidly deployable treatment solutions that help utilities move from initial evaluation through long-term operation.
